requirements.requirement: Every sudo command run on node1 is recorded to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the user and a timestamp
requirements.summary: cmd-b7564bfa4eb04093 shows /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging with Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log", log_year, log_host, validated via visudo -cf. Test sudo commands (chmod, visudo, touch, chown, whoami, id, cat) appear in sudo-commands.log with format 'TIMESTAMP YEAR : user : HOST=node1 : TTY=... ; PWD=... ; USER=root ; COMMAND=...', satisfying user+timestamp capture. cmd-ba5312a62b7b4711 confirms a fresh post-reboot sudo command (hostname) is also correctly logged, showing the configuration is durable.

requirements.requirement: Those sudo command entries are kept out of the general system log (auth.log/journal)
requirements.summary: cmd-b7564bfa4eb04093 applies Defaults !syslog and the post-change auth.log tail/journal grep show no new COMMAND= session-body lines for the test commands. cmd-ba5312a62b7b4711 and cmd-cdc73656b6164091 show that after reboot, grep of auth.log for COMMAND= yields only 13 pre-existing matches, and inspection of those matches confirms they are a pre-task setup entry and two entries timestamped exactly at 09:16:16 that occurred before the sudoers drop-in took effect (the baseline 'tail -5 auth.log' call and the 'tee' call that wrote the drop-in itself, both necessarily logged under the prior configuration). journalctl -b for the post-reboot boot shows zero COMMAND= entries. This directly demonstrates no leakage once the config is active.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrating full pre/post recovery on node1 (independent of public contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline boot_id (b185f188...) and healthy sudoers/log state captured (cmd-8f726ee93e564311); reboot acknowledged via background-delayed systemctl reboot (cmd-2bd4cb4294ee4bd7); node observed unreachable (cmd-e1cce210f22a4989, cmd-fac369ccef904320) then reachable with a new boot_id (85b662c9..., cmd-0f03f07678be4483), matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot; post-restart verification (cmd-ba5312a62b7b4711) shows sudoers file intact/valid, log file persists, and a fresh sudo command logs correctly with continued syslog suppression.

overall_summary: The executor correctly implemented sudo command logging to /var/log/sudo-commands.log (with user and timestamp) via a validated /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging drop-in using logfile/log_year/log_host plus !syslog to suppress entries from auth.log and the journal. Both material requirements are directly demonstrated with before/after evidence, including proof that the only remaining COMMAND= lines in auth.log predate the configuration taking effect. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed cleanly: baseline boot identity and healthy state, reboot acknowledgement, unreachable-then-reachable transition, a new boot identity, and full post-restart recovery of the sudoers config, log file, and correct logging/suppression behavior. Operational hygiene is clean with no unnecessary or unreverted mutations.
limitations: The auth.log grep count of 13 COMMAND= matches was not fully itemized beyond the three shown lines (one pre-task setup entry plus two at 09:16:16); the remaining ~10 matches were not individually inspected, though timestamps and context strongly imply they all predate the config change.
Journal verification of no-leakage was scoped to the current boot (journalctl -b) and a 20-line recent-journal grep pre-restart, not an exhaustive review of the full journal history.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands are directly tied to the task: creating and validating the sudoers drop-in, setting safe (0600 root:root) permissions on the new log file, running a small number of test sudo commands to verify logging behavior, and a single controlled reboot required for the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations were found; the after_executor vs after_prepare diff shows only the expected boot-id change and reboot-driven systemd-private temp directory churn, not executor residue. No troubleshooting dead-ends or reverted experiments appear in the timeline.
